content.text:
I fixed the uber-jar build in `UberJarBuilder.java` so it no longer closes dependency path trees too early. I couldn't compile or run any tests here: Maven can't resolve the BOM imports offline, so the change has not been compiled or tested.

**Cause:** `walkFileDependencyForDependency` opened each dependency's path tree and closed it as soon as the walk finished. The uber-jar writer only queues lazy `Files.newInputStream(path)` suppliers during the walk. It reads the actual content later in `ParallelCommonsCompressArchiveCreator.close()`, on worker threads. In a multi-threaded Maven build, other modules share the same cached path trees. By the time the content was read, the shared zip filesystem could be closed, which gives `ClosedFileSystemException`.

**Fix:** The opened trees are now collected in a list and closed only after the archive creator has closed. The closer is declared as the first resource in the try-with-resources, so it runs last. `walkFileDependencyForDependency` takes the list as a new parameter.

I did not check whether `copyApplicationContent` has the same pattern. It may be worth a look.
